title: Risotto con Vongole
subtitle: Clam risotto with white wine and parsley
excerpt: Risotto con vongole is a briny, elegant risotto made with fresh clams, white wine, and parsley. The clams open in wine and the liquor they release goes into the risotto as part of the cooking liquid. The result is intensely savoury and oceanic. Like most Italian seafood risotto, it is not finished with Parmesan.
sourceNotes: Clam risotto is a classic of the Veneto and coastal Lazio. The technique of opening clams in wine and using the liquor as part of the risotto stock is standard across the Italian Adriatic and Tyrrhenian coastlines.

content.text: The key step is opening the clams in wine in a separate pan before starting the risotto. This gives you clam liquor, which is salty and powerfully flavoured, and the opened clams to add at the end. Taste the clam liquor before adding it: if very salty, dilute with some of the fish or chicken stock.

items.prepNote: taste before adding; the clam liquor is salty

content.text: Place {{clams}} clams in a wide pan with half the {{white-wine-dry}} wine. Cover and cook over a high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until the clams open. Discard any that stay closed. Strain the liquor through a fine sieve and reserve. Remove most clams from their shells, keeping a few in shell for serving.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{chilli-flakes}} chilli flakes (if using) and cook for 1 minute.

Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the remaining {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed. Begin adding the clam liquor and {{chicken-stock}} stock combined, a ladleful at a time, stirring and waiting for each addition to absorb. Continue for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente.
Stir in the clam meat, taste for {{salt-table}} salt, and add {{parsley-flat}} parsley. Serve immediately, with the reserved clams in shell arranged on top.

items.cause: The clam liquor was not diluted enough.
items.fix: Taste the clam liquor before adding it. If very salty, use more chicken stock and less clam liquor. The clams themselves add salt at the end, so keep the risotto underseasoned until the clams are stirred in.

content.text: Clam risotto is found along the whole Italian Adriatic coast, from Venice down to Puglia. In Venice it is made with vongole veraci (carpet-shell clams), which are sweet and tender. The dish is never served with Parmesan -- in Italian coastal cooking, cheese is not added to seafood pasta or risotto. It is a summer and autumn dish, following the season of the vongole.
